# Bank Transfer Process Clause

Defines when a Bank Transfer Contract may request its single bank transfer. `paymentPolicyAction` is `transfer`. The clause controls requests; only the bank's confirmed outcome records transferred money. It provides no synthetic card authorization or capture, and a refund is a separate transfer instruction.

## Configuration and conditions

Parameters are read from the clause in its executing document, which must be a Bank Transfer Contract. All paths below belong to that document, including when it is a nested instruction.

- `parameters.method` defaults to `bank-transfer`; `conditional-bank` is also accepted. Other values are rejected. Both accepted values use the same transfer policy behavior shown here.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to an empty object. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`, leaving requests to the contract's explicit `requestTransfer` operation without adding conditional automation.
- `parameters.transfer.mode: when` requires `when`, the condition expression, and a nonempty text `requestId` for the automatic request. Execution requires every transfer request identifier to be 1–128 characters.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to an empty object. A condition reading `/sources/<alias>/...` must declare that alias here; the supplied definitions do not establish the source connection configuration in full.

Conditions support static `$document` paths, comparisons, Boolean operations, existence and inclusion checks, size, addition, subtraction and literals. Document paths must start with `/` and cannot be `/` alone. Dynamic paths, unsupported operators, undeclared source aliases and expressions exceeding the bounded nesting scan are rejected.

In `when` mode, the clause initializes `/paymentProcess_<clauseKey>/transferAllowed` to `false` and points `/paymentTerms/transferGate` to it. A different existing `transferGate` causes a configuration conflict. The gate becomes true only when `/activation/active` is exactly true, the condition evaluates to exactly true, and either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly true.

Changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and the condition's document dependencies trigger reevaluation; declared sources also add a source-event handler. Automatic requesting additionally requires `/payment/accepted` to be true, `/payment/closed` to be explicitly false and `/bankTransfer/status` to be `idle`. An open gate alone does not establish these conditions or confirm payment. Policy transitions are rejected with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

## Requests and bank outcomes

`requestTransfer` is declared on `payer` and checks the calling channel against `/paymentTerms/payerChannel`. It accepts only `requestId`; the amount and currency come from `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` and `/paymentTerms/currency`. Automatic requests use the configured identifier and bypass this caller-channel check, while retaining acceptance, source-readiness and transfer-gate checks.

A new request requires an accepted instruction, ready document sources when configured, a payment not marked closed, and any configured transfer gate to resolve to exactly true. It records `/bankTransfer/requestId`, sets `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested`, and emits a Bank Transfer Event with `kind: Transfer Requested`, `requestId`, `amountMinor` and `currency`. This records an attempt, not money transferred.

Once an identifier is recorded, the same identifier returns `duplicate` after the source, caller and acceptance checks, without rechecking closure or the gate. A different identifier is rejected; this process does not start a second transfer.

`confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer` and `reportTransferUnknown` are declared on `guarantor` and require the calling channel to match `/paymentTerms/guarantorChannel`. Each requires the recorded `requestId` and a bank `reference` of 1–256 characters. Confirmation additionally requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to exactly match `paymentTerms`. Decline and unknown reports may omit those two fields; supplied values are not checked for equality by the shown recording logic. Other business input fields are rejected.

A new outcome may replace `requested` or `unknown`. It records status and reference and emits `Transfer Outcome`. Thus `unknown` remains unresolved and can later become `completed` or `declined` for the same request. Completed and declined outcomes are final. Retrying the same status and reference returns `duplicate`; a changed reference for that status or a different outcome after finality is rejected.

Confirmation sets `/payment/completed` to the full `paymentTerms.amountMinor`, stores the bank reference in `/payment/transactionId`, and emits Payment Completed with `amountCompleted`, `evidence: bankConfirmation`, `reference` and `requestId`. Amounts are integer minor units of `paymentTerms.currency`; the completed value is neither a reservation nor a net-of-refunds total. Decline and unknown outcomes do not record completed money.

Public operations also invoke `Require Active Parties`; its detailed checks are not supplied. Other runtime initialization is not established here, so missing state must not be interpreted as `idle`, false, zero or completion.
